source.title: LoopFM: Learning frOm HistOrical RePresentations of Foundation Model for Recommendation
source.authors: Hua Zheng; Shali Jiang; Boyang Liu; Laming Chen; Kenny Lov; Chuanqi Xu; Lisang Ding; Qinghai Zhou; Can Cui; Xiaolong Liu; Xiaoyi Liu; Yasmine Badr; Xin Xu; Mingfu Liang; Jiyan Yang; Ellie Dingqiao Wen; Gerard Jonathan Mugisha Akkerhuis; Jason Rudy; Xi Liu; Chenxiao Guan; Rong Jin; Ruichao Qiu; Xian Chen; Zhehui Zhou; Ping Chen; Rui Yang; Haicheng Chen; Meet Raval; Song Zhou; Dharak Kharod; Shuyu Xu; Xingyuan Wang; Liang Tao; Qiang Jin; Qiao Yang; Wankun Zhu; Qin Huang; Yuzhen Huang; Darren Liu; Parish Aggarwal; Hui Zhou; Erzhuo Wang; Shuo Chang; Xiaorui Gan; Wenlin Chen; Santanu Kolay; Huayu Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports scaling results for recommendation-system models, but does not test the claimed language-model pretraining loss laws, their extrapolation, or their compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own recommendation-system scaling results, including relative NE gain versus FM compute and recommendation AUC across FM capacities. These are not held-out language-model pretraining losses or measurements of any listed version, so the rows are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: This is a recommendation-system knowledge-transfer paper. Its 'scaling law' results are (a) relative NE gain of a downstream vertical model plotted against upstream FM compute, figure only, four points and no fitted exponent, and (b) AUC of DMIN variants from 1.9M to 31.5M parameters. Neither measures held-out pretraining loss of the scaled model. Neither concerns language models, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture shape at fixed size. The NE-gain-vs-compute plot is a transfer-gain metric for a different model, not the loss-scaling form named in V5. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that LoopFM's transfer gains grow with sequence length, with FM scale (power-law-like versus FM compute internally), and with embedding dimension when the sequence encoder is wide enough. They also conclude that it roughly doubles the KD transfer ratio in production. Note that their public FM-capacity sweep shows no systematic trend, which they acknowledge may not represent industrial scale.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies recommendation-system representation transfer, not the methods or measurements in the cited language-model scaling-law sources.
record.method_sensitivity: For the paper's recommendation results, embedding dimension gains depend on downstream sequence-encoder capacity; its public FM-capacity sweep reports no systematic trend in ΔAUC with FM size.

fits_no_version.finding: For internal trillion-parameter recommendation FMs (0.84–5.0×10^23 FLOPs), the downstream VM's relative NE gain from LoopFM rises with FM compute. The authors describe it as a predictable power law, with no fitted exponent or uncertainty given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In FM-to-VM recommendation transfer, the downstream gain from transferred embeddings grows predictably (approximately power-law) with upstream FM training compute.

fits_no_version.finding: On TaobaoAd, KD+LoopFM AUC across DMIN FMs of 1.9M–31.5M parameters ranges 0.6243–0.6284, and ΔAUC over KD ranges 0.0332–0.0380 with no systematic size trend. Standalone DMIN AUC saturates at 31–65M parameters and degrades beyond, which the authors attribute to overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-scale recommendation models show little or no monotone benefit from FM scale, with saturation and degradation beyond tens of millions of parameters.

record.problems: The scaling results use recommendation-system metrics, not language-model pretraining loss. Figure 2 gives no stated fitted exponent or uncertainty. The public capacity sweep spans 1.9M–31.5M parameters, and the authors caution that it may not represent industrial systems.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed claim versions were reported. Results about sequence length, embedding dimensions, transfer methods, and other recommendation ablations were not included because they do not test the claimed language-model scaling behavior.

untested.parts: All: no language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no extrapolation of fitted laws to larger runs.
All: no parameter/token allocation under fixed compute.
All: no depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
No loss-versus-scale power law for the recommendation FM itself. Only a downstream transfer-gain plot (figure only) and AUC tables.
All: no language-model downstream task results.
All: no comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: There is an internal inconsistency: Section 4 cites Table 10 as showing an 'AUC spread < 0.001 across 16× FM capacity', but Appendix G reports a KD+LoopFM spread of 0.0041. The paper does not cite the original LM scaling-law sources; its scaling references are recommendation-system ones (Wukong, Kunlun, LLaTTE). Taking V5's 'transfer' clause literally, a reviewer might consider r1, but the measure is another model's gain, shown in a figure only with no fit, so it cannot support or challenge V5.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from fits on small runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between language-model parameters and training tokens.
Effects of language-model depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the claimed loss scaling form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the paper's recommendation-system scaling metrics do not measure the named loss behavior.
Predictability of language-model downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Whether language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with fitting choices or curves bend away from power laws.

rows.measure: Relative NE gain of LoopFM versus FM compute
rows.note: The authors describe the result as a predictable power-law relationship. The plotted performance values and any fitted exponent are not stated in the text; this is recommendation-system NE gain, not language-model pretraining loss.
rows.check: Measure is the downstream VM's relative NE gain from LoopFM versus FM compute, not the scaled model's own loss. Values are figure only. The power-law description is the authors' wording with no stated fit, so 'observed' overstates what can be read.
